text.p: Thousands of Christians thronged All Saints Cathedral in Nairobi on Sunday when Anglican Archbishop David Gitari led a ceremonial "cleansing" and re-dedication after last week's riots in the Kenyan capital.

Riot police threw teargas and beat worshippers with batons when people fleeing a confrontation between demonstrators and police took refuge in the cathedral last Monday. Senior police officials later publicly apologised for the invasion.
The demonstrations, called to back opposition calls for constitutional reforms ahead of elections due to be held later this year, went ahead in several towns despite a government ban.
The cathedral cancelled all services after Monday's clashes, pending a ceremonial re-dedication.
On Sunday Archbishop Gitari led a team of Anglican priests round the packed cathedral, praying at the bloodstains which bore witness to the riots.
Hundreds of Christians, crowded out of the building, surrounded the cathedral and joined in the service, relayed by loudspeakers.

They applauded the Reverend Timothy Njoya, a Presbyterian and a vocal opposition supporter, who was admitted to hospital with injuries after being beaten in the cathedral last week. Njoya and representatives of other Christian denominations joined in the service.
